title: Part Two, Chapter 4: Xquic in the House of Xmucane

verses.t: And the mother of Hun-batz and Hun-choven was at home when the woman called Xquic arrived; then the woman called Xquic came to the mother of Hun-batz and Hun-choven, and she was already pregnant, and only a little time was left before the birth of Hun-ahpu and Xbalanque, as they were called. And when this woman came to the old woman, the woman Xquic said to her, "I have come, lady mother; I am your daughter-in-law and your little daughter." This she said when she came to the old woman. "Where do you come from? Are my sons alive? Did they not die there in the underworld? Are not those who are my descendants, called Hun-batz and Hun-choven, here? Where do you come from? Get out of here!" said the old woman to the maiden. "Only this is true: that I am your daughter-in-law, and I belong to Hun-hun-ahpu, and this is what I carry. They live; Hun-hun-ahpu and Vucub-hun-ahpu are not dead. What they have done is only a sentence upon themselves, in the light, lady mother-in-law, and so you shall see them again in what I carry," she said to the old woman. And at this Hun-batz and Hun-choven grew angry, who did nothing but play the flute and sing, paint and carve all day, and were the old woman's comfort. And she said, "In no way do I want you as my daughter-in-law, for what you carry in your womb is from fornication. You are a deceiver, for my sons that you speak of are dead." And the old woman said, "What I have told you is true; but very well, my daughter-in-law, I hear what you say to me. So go and fetch food; go and harvest a big net of it, and then come back, since you are my daughter-in-law, as I hear," it was said to the maiden. "Very well," she said, and then she went to the cornfield that Hun-batz and Hun-choven had, and there was the broad path that they had made. The maiden followed it and came to the cornfield; but she found only one stalk of maize, not two or three stalks, and it had no ears. And then the maiden was troubled: "Oh, sinner that I am! Where am I to get a net of food, as they ask of me?" And she said, "I shall call and invoke the one who guards the food, that she may come: Xtoh, Xcanil, Xcanix, you who guard our sustenance; Hun-batz and Hun-choven!" This is what the maiden said. And then she took hold of the silk of the ear and pulled it out, and did not take the ear; and as soon as she arranged it in the net, the net filled up with ears of maize and became a great netful. And then the maiden came back; but animals carried the net as she came. And she went to deliver her load; and when she appeared at the house, she came as if with a load. And when the old woman saw it, as soon as she saw that great net of food, she said, "Where did you get this? Have you finished carrying off our whole cornfield? I shall go and see it first," said the old woman. And then she went to see the cornfield, and so she found her one stalk of maize, and it was also plain where the net had been. And then at once the old woman came back and arrived at her house, and said to the maiden, "This sign alone is enough to know that you are my daughter-in-law. I shall see your deeds, and those of the ones you carry, who are wise," it was said to the maiden.
